newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed, Raytheon,TRW venture seeks Pentagon pact.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed, Raytheon,TRW venture seeks Pentagon pact.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp, Raytheon Co and TRW Inc's newly formed missile venture is seeking a U.S. defense contract with a potential value in the billions of dollars over many years, spokespersons for the venture said.

While spokespersons declined to call it the return of the Strategic Defense Initiative or "Star Wars" program that was proposed during the Reagan years, the venture will use much of the technology developed for missile defense.
Blanche Necessary, a manager for communications for United Missile Defense Co, said value of the program has not been determined, but depends on the federal budget.

United Missile Defense Co venture is responding to a study commissioned by the U.S. Ballistic Missile Defense Organization for a missile defense program, Bob Hayden, business manager for the venture, said. The agency is expected to make study awards on May 1, 1997.
Competitors include Boeing Co, which is merging with McDonnell Douglas Corp and recently acquired Rockwell International Corp's defense business.

"This is not thought to be an impenetrable shield," Hayden said about the missile defense program. "That is not where we're headed. We're talking about small numbers of missiles and accidental launches."
The Strategic Defense Initiative was devised to be an impenetrable shield from missiles -- a multi-billion dollar plan that was centered on blocking missiles from the former Soviet Union.
Raytheon, Lockheed Martin and TRW are going to continue their separate missile businesses, Hayden said.
Hayden said the venture is a sign of greater cooperation in the defense industry, because of the decreased number of companies remaining in the defense industry.
The contract for the study of a missile defense system is $8 million, Hayden said.
Hayden said the Clinton Administration is proposing a missile defense program that could be off the drawing board by the year 2000 and completed by 2003.
The system would include ground-based radar, control and command, satellites and interceptor missiles, Hayden said.
Raytheon's specialty is ground-based radar, and most of work would be completed in Massachusetts.
Lockheed Martin would contribute its expertise in strategic missiles with work being completed in Sunnyvale, Calif. and Huntsville, Ala., Necessary said.
TRW is contributing its background systems integration with the work being completed in San Bernadino, Calif. and Sunnyvale, Calif. and in the Washington DC area, Necessary said.
